results.title: Removing T2375 changes eleven to twelve
results.brief: At the final input “is”, removing L29–T2375 changes the initial answers November→December, K→L and XI→XII in three selected raw prompts.

results.title: Where the gate activates—and where it does not
results.brief: T2375 activates at final “is” in the original eleven templates. Matched first, second, fourth and fifth month/Roman prefixes have zero gate there.

results.title: Activation does not guarantee an answer flip
results.brief: The eleventh-element prompt has an active T2375 contribution but retains Sodium after removal. The effect is not a general next-item operation.

results.title: Similar directions, different magnitudes
results.brief: Month, alphabet and Roman contributions have cosine similarities of 0.983–0.989, with different lengths. High alignment also occurs in cases without a flip.

results.title: Related activity and geometry across five languages
results.brief: Matched chat setups show highly aligned month contributions across five languages. Activation varies with wording and format, and can occur on chat-prefix tokens.

results.title: Causal transfer depends on language and format
results.brief: Some translated prompts shift to twelve, others retain eleven. Some alphabet questions shift K→N rather than K→L. This is not a universal multilingual rule.

results.title: A stronger scalar can make the fifth-month answer start November
results.brief: Copying the natural eleventh-month gate leaves May unchanged. Larger tested gates produce November initially, followed by self-correction.

results.title: Borrowing the donor operator still requires amplification
results.brief: Copying the natural full contribution leaves May unchanged. Amplification can produce an initial November; equal-norm recipient controls can do so too.

results.title: The month steering result does not carry over to the fifth element
results.brief: Across 17 scalar settings, no initial Sodium or Aluminum answer appears. Native fifth-, eleventh- and thirteenth-element capability checks all pass.

results.title: Direct vocabulary readouts do not explain all three flips
results.brief: Readouts of the MLP, removed contribution and remainder weaken the eleven preference, but do not fully reproduce the complete model’s alphabet/Roman flips.

results.title: Twelve is not always the native runner-up
results.brief: December is already a strong competitor; L is outside the alphabet top five. The edit also changes relative preferences beyond simply removing eleven’s probability.

results.title: Only T2375 flips the month among six active L29 controls
results.brief: Each naturally active transform is removed separately. The five other removals preserve the initial November answer, including some larger contribution edits.

results.title: T1181 removal counteracts the December result
results.brief: Removing L29–T1181 together with T2375 restores an initial November. On a genuine twelfth-month prompt, T1181 removal lowers December probability without flipping it.

results.title: The perturbation propagates through later layers
results.brief: Absolute vector distance grows after the L29 edit. Residual directions stay relatively close, and their angular separation does not grow monotonically.

results.title: Different downstream gates change across domains
results.brief: The month, alphabet and Roman prompts have different gate changes. The four month-case switches stay inactive at final “is” in the other two prompts.

results.title: Alphabet examples reveal before-K down and before-L up
results.brief: Three gates with before-K examples weaken; two with before-L examples strengthen. Roman examples suggest broader numeral/X/I contexts, without clear XII specificity.

results.title: T2375 and T1468 often coactivate, with clear exceptions
results.brief: Across 56 prompts, 43 token pairs have both gates active, 21 only T2375 and two only T1468. Correlation among the 66 plotted nonzero pairs is 0.39.

results.title: T1468 does not reproduce or rescue the flip
results.brief: T1468 removal alone causes no eleven→twelve flips. During T2375 ablation, restoring its native scalar or full contribution rescues 0/3 initial answers.
